StatusLIVE EXECUTIVE DASHBOARD
PurposeFounder-level command board for actual-versus-plan variance, milestone slippage, recovery quality, live-gate discipline drift, and decision resets needed to keep the quarter governable.
Source ruleUpdate quarterly plan, strategic initiatives, assumption control, owner accountability, weekly review, monthly review, KPI scorecard, executable-check control board, and linked source records first, then refresh this review.
Founder useConvert early drift into owned recovery action before ambition becomes revisionism or founder rescue becomes the hidden plan.
Protection ruleThis dashboard governs recovery posture only; approved templates, brand assets, and source-record protections stay unchanged.

Recovery Control PostureLink

Control lensCurrent postureFounder readRequired response
Quarter recoverabilityRecoverable if the next 30 days are managed as a correction window, not a narrative update cycle.The plan is still viable, but drift must be treated early.Keep every material variance tied to owner, cause, recovery move, evidence route, and dated proof.
Variance concentrationCash discipline, diversification, sourcing depth, and live-gate behavior carry the largest drift.The weak points are connected; one soft assumption can affect several commitments.Route variance through assumption control, cash, capital, and owner-accountability surfaces together.
Founder-rescue exposureTrust-linked same-day gates still reveal the largest operating-behavior gap.A quarter cannot be called controlled if founder intervention is the fallback control.Convert founder-rescued gates into executable-check recovery and owner-accountability evidence.
Recovery qualityRecovery moves are named, but proof standards need sharper graduation and stop rules.Activity is not recovery unless it changes the next decision.Reject recovery updates that lack source-board movement, KPI evidence, or decision-ready proof.
Capital and release protectionVariance can distort cash, release, concession, and capacity decisions if not contained.Soft recovery language can quietly consume scarce resources.Require capital-allocation review before widening any commitment affected by unresolved variance.

Variance Severity TiersLink

Severity tierConditionFounder postureRequired control action
MonitorVariance is visible but does not yet affect cash, release, customer promise, or founder workload.Watch without overreacting.Keep owner, date, and source route current.
CorrectVariance affects a quarter priority but has a credible recovery path and no hidden exposure.Push harder and require proof.Add dated recovery evidence and KPI movement before next review.
ContainVariance could distort cash, release, capacity, concession, or trust-linked movement.Stop expansion until proof improves.Route to capital allocation, assumption control, and source board containment.
EscalateVariance repeats after founder pressure or creates same-day operating risk.Treat as owner-rhythm or control-system failure.Route to owner accountability, executable-check control, and founder decision board.
ResetVariance invalidates the commitment or makes the original plan misleading.Replace the plan language rather than defending it.Update quarterly plan, forecast, scenario response, and founder decisions.

Recovery Evidence StandardLink

Recovery proof typeMinimum evidenceInvalid substituteFounder read
Cash recoveryUpdated cash forecast, collection status, release posture, and owner action date.General confidence that payment will arrive.Cash-sensitive recovery is real only when it changes exposure control.
Demand diversificationPipeline stage movement, qualification proof, next dated customer action, and concentration impact.A new prospect name without stage discipline.Diversification is not real until it reduces anchor-account dependence.
Supply recoveryBackup-source proof, capacity confirmation, scenario path, and promise-window adjustment.Verbal supplier comfort or theoretical capacity.Sourcing recovery must protect committed demand before upside.
Live-gate recoveryCurrent executable-check record, owner-led closeout proof, funding-release posture, and no founder-rescue repeat.Founder availability at the moment of risk.Live-gate recovery exists only when the system acts before founder rescue.
Pricing recoveryQuote evidence, margin impact, concession reason, recovery route, and founder-decision status.Commercial urgency or relationship rationale alone.Pricing recovery must protect realized margin, not just win probability.

Escalation and Stop RulesLink

RuleConditionRequired escalationFounder action
Stale recovery stopRecovery update lacks current source evidence, owner date, or KPI movement.Route to owner accountability and reject narrative status.Keep variance open and require proof before next review.
Founder-rescue repeatSame variance or gate requires founder intervention twice in one cycle.Route to owner accountability, executable-check control, and founder decision board.Intensify, narrow scope, or reset owner expectation.
Capital containment stopRecovery asks for cash, release, concession, or capacity while proof remains weak.Route to capital allocation, cash forecast, and relevant source board.Pause expansion until capital posture is reconciled.
Forecast reset triggerForecast confidence remains high after validation date slips or assumption proof weakens.Route to revenue forecast, assumption control, and quarterly plan.Reset confidence band and update plan language.
Scenario activation triggerVariance threatens supply, payment, release, or counterparty timing.Route to scenario response and risk register.Activate fallback path or containment language.
